subject: Catalyst demo — recommended shortlist & next steps

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liz Carter <liz.carter@catalyst.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Catalyst demo — recommended shortlist & next steps

Hi Liz — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our side and a recommended slate to move toward a short pilot.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary goal: generate concise product summaries from long-form support transcripts (avg 3–5k tokens), target P95 latency <= 800ms for inline UX.
- Quality bar: F1 > 0.85 on entity extraction checks and < 6% hallucination rate on factual checks.
- Traffic: expected 150k monthly requests initially, spike-friendly during releases.
- Regulatory note: data must remain in us-east-1; Catalyst requires audit log export for preview tokens.

Recommended shortlist (prioritized):
1) redwood-llama-3-medium-quant (best cost/throughput balance) — strong at instruction-following prompts, quantized variant reduces GPU op cost by ~45%.
2) open-rt-7b (low-latency variant) — good P95 latency at 1k token budgets for shorter summaries; slightly higher hallucination risk on long context.
3) alpine-13b-v1 (quality-first fallback) — highest accuracy on long transcripts but heavier on cost/latency; keep as canary for high-value records.

Attached: prompt pack we used in the demo + a simple latency vs cost projection for the three candidates.

Next steps I propose:
- We run a 2-week eval on a 2k-sample prompt set (we can provision sandboxed dedicated capacity in us-east-1).
- Redwood provides a lightweight eval harness (we'll seed it with your test transcripts) and a regression guardrail for hallucination checks.
- We sync 7 days after you confirm to finalize procurement and pilot sizing.

Would love a quick yes/no on the shortlist and whether Catalyst can share a small labeled set (200 transcripts) for the initial eval.

Thanks — Hannah

hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0192

Hannah / Marissa — benchmark + cost sketch attached (see latency-cost-sheet.xlsx) and quick notes below. I ran 50-sample runs at 3k and 5k token budgets in our sandbox (us-east-1). Raw numbers are noisy but directional.

Bench highlights (50-sample per model):
- redwood-llama-3-medium-quant:
  P50 (3k): 420ms | P95 (3k): 740ms
  P50 (5k): 620ms | P95 (5k): 1,150ms (note: quant kernels degrade on long KV chains)
  Quality: hallucination ~5.5% on our prompt set; entity-exact F1: 0.83

- open-rt-7b:
  P50 (3k): 360ms | P95 (3k): 680ms
  P50 (5k): 580ms | P95 (5k): 980ms
  Quality: hallucination ~7.2%; entity F1: 0.79

- alpine-13b-v1:
  P50 (3k): 810ms | P95 (3k): 1,450ms
  P50 (5k): 1,100ms | P95 (5k): 1,950ms
  Quality: hallucination ~2.1%; entity F1: 0.90

Cost sketch (approx monthly for 150k requests, avg 800 tokens per request):
- redwood-llama-3-medium-quant: $9k–$12k
- open-rt-7b: $12k–$16k
- alpine-13b-v1: $36k–$48k

Recommendation rationale:
- Start the pilot with redwood-llama-3-medium-quant, but gate rollouts by hallucination regressions on a sampled review set. The medium quant hits P95 target for 3k inputs and is the best cost compromise.
- Keep open-rt-7b in the pool for latency-sensitive endpoints that can tolerate slightly lower quality.
- Use alpine-13b-v1 as a fallback for high-value records and for nightly batch processing where latency is less critical.

Risks & mitigations:
- If P95 for 5k remains >1s on the quant path, we should trigger automatic routing to open-rt-7b or to a sharded alpine instance for that request type.
- Implement prefix-KV caching for users with repetitive transcript structure (saves ~30% tokens).

I attached the XLS with per-run histograms and cost calculations.

Ben

Liz — thanks for the quick turnaround and for offering the sample set. Attaching the same prompt pack and an eval harness link; below is a tightened recommendation and pilot plan based on Ben's bench.

Tightened shortlist & pilot plan:
- Pilot model: redwood-llama-3-medium-quant (primary) — meets P95 for ~3k inputs and is lowest cost. We'll run the 2-week eval on your 200-sample set and report per-case failures.
- Latency fallback: open-rt-7b — automatically routed for requests where quant P95 > 1s.
- Quality fallback: alpine-13b-v1 — nightly batch for edge/high-value records and for adjudication.

Regression guardrail (what you'll see):
- Automated sampling: 1% of live requests streamed to an eval job for hallucination checks (factuality heuristics + entity match).
- Dashboard: per-prompt regression trendline, rolling 7-day hallucination rate, and ability to open a review ticket per example.
- Alerting: we set a threshold at +2% absolute hallucination regression to trigger a canary rollback.

Pilot logistics:
- Catalyst provides the 200-transcript anonymized sample (drop into the Drive folder) by end of day tomorrow.
- Redwood will provision sandbox (us-east-1) and run evals + bench within 48 hours of receipt.
- We sync 1 week into the pilot to decide production sizing.
